name: Cultural Center of the Philippines

meta.title: Cultural Center of the Philippines — CROIX
meta.description: Honouring and highlighting an iconic national landmark through complete exterior and interior lighting design, testing, and fixture selection.

scope: Exterior + interior lighting design, testing, and fixture selection
summary: Honouring and highlighting an iconic national landmark through complete exterior and interior lighting design, testing, and fixture selection.
context: The Cultural Center of the Philippines is one of the country’s most recognisable civic buildings. The commission covered the full exterior and interior lighting scope, with testing and fixture selection included rather than left to a separate supplier.
approach: Heritage work begins with restraint: the light should reveal the building’s fabric and proportion, not compete with it. The scope combined exterior façade studies, interior lighting design, on-site testing, and a fixture selection process documented for approval and handover.

name: North–South Commuter Railway, Malolos–Clark CP N-03
menuTitle: North–South Commuter Railway, Malolos–Clark CP N-03

meta.title: North–South Commuter Railway, Malolos–Clark CP N-03 — CROIX
meta.description: Designing safe, reliable station, platform, building façade, and road lighting for a major national train network.

scope: Station, platform, building façade, and road lighting
summary: Designing safe, reliable station, platform, building façade, and road lighting for a major national train network.
context: The North–South Commuter Railway is a national transport programme. The lighting scope covered the passenger-facing environments — stations, platforms, façades — as well as the roads that connect them.
approach: Transport lighting is a life-safety system as much as a design one. Illuminance, uniformity, emergency egress, glare, and maintainability drive the layout; the visual result follows from those constraints rather than fighting them.

name: Arena di Verona

meta.title: Arena di Verona — CROIX
meta.description: Lighting one of Italy’s most treasured ancient Roman amphitheaters with care and drama.

scope: Architectural lighting design for an ancient Roman amphitheatre
summary: Lighting one of Italy’s most treasured ancient Roman amphitheaters with care and drama.
context: The Arena di Verona is a working opera house and a fragile Roman monument. The lighting had to serve performance, visitors, and the preservation of the original stone.
approach: The design balances drama with conservation: controlled beams, warm colour temperatures, and careful aiming keep the light on the architecture rather than in the sky. The work was developed in collaboration with Voltaire Light Design.

name: Our Habitas AlUla

meta.title: Our Habitas AlUla — CROIX
meta.description: Creating an intimate, star-friendly nighttime atmosphere for a world-famous desert sanctuary.

scope: Nighttime atmosphere and lighting design for a desert resort
summary: Creating an intimate, star-friendly nighttime atmosphere for a world-famous desert sanctuary.
context: Our Habitas AlUla sits in a desert landscape where the night sky is part of the guest experience. The lighting had to support hospitality, wayfinding, and the character of the terrain without washing out the stars.
approach: The scheme works in the low end of the lighting range: warm, low-glare sources; careful shielding; and a hierarchy that lets the desert recede into darkness. The work was developed in collaboration with Voltaire Light Design.

name: Benetton Group Headquarters

meta.title: Benetton Group Headquarters — CROIX
meta.description: Delivering clean, modern workplace and architectural lighting for a global fashion icon.

summary: Delivering clean, modern workplace and architectural lighting for a global fashion icon.
context: The Benetton headquarters in Treviso is a workplace and a brand environment. The lighting needed to support long occupancy, visual comfort, and the clarity of the architecture.
approach: Workplace lighting balances vertical illuminance, glare control, and control zoning. The design keeps the ceiling legible, gives the interior a calm rhythm, and allows the lighting to shift with the working day. The work was developed in collaboration with Voltaire Light Design.

name: Hotel Aldrovandi & Sheraton Spa

meta.title: Hotel Aldrovandi & Sheraton Spa — CROIX
meta.description: Shaping calm, restorative hotel and spa environments in two of Italy’s most famous destinations.

summary: Shaping calm, restorative hotel and spa environments in two of Italy’s most famous destinations.
context: Two hospitality settings, two different atmospheres: a city hotel in Rome and a spa in Como. Both depend on lighting that lowers the visual temperature and makes the guest experience feel unhurried.
approach: The design uses layered, low-glare light: warm pools of illumination, soft vertical washes, and scenes that transition from arrival to rest. The work was developed in collaboration with In-visible lab.

name: JW Marriott Hotel, Jeju Island

meta.title: JW Marriott Hotel, Jeju Island — CROIX
meta.description: Elevating luxury guest experiences through specialist lighting design review alongside Sergio Boccia Lighting Design.

summary: Elevating luxury guest experiences through specialist lighting design review alongside Sergio Boccia Lighting Design.
context: A luxury resort project with an established design team. CROIX’s role was a specialist lighting design review rather than a full turnkey appointment.
approach: The review focused on the guest-facing lighting layers: arrival, lobby, dining, and spa. The aim was to protect the design intent, check glare and colour consistency, and give the lighting team a clear set of decisions to carry into documentation.

name: Signature Retail & Dining

meta.title: Signature Retail & Dining — CROIX
meta.description: Complete turnkey lighting design for IAI Restaurant in BGC, SMEG Showrooms, and Mobelhaus Showrooms.

scope: Turnkey lighting design for IAI Restaurant, SMEG, and Mobelhaus showrooms
summary: Complete turnkey lighting design for IAI Restaurant in BGC, SMEG Showrooms, and Mobelhaus Showrooms.
context: A cluster of retail and dining environments in Taguig, each with a different product story: food, appliances, and furniture. The scope was turnkey lighting design across the group.
approach: Retail lighting is merchandising: beam angles, contrast, and colour rendering are tuned to the product and the material. Dining adds another layer — the room has to feel good before the food arrives. The work was delivered as a single turnkey scope across the venues.
